FACULTY SENATE LEGISLATION May 7, 2026 Graduate Council Report 2025-2026-7A After the April 6, 2026 meeting of the Graduate Council, the following matters were considered and virtually voted on and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval.
Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation By The Faculty Senate COURSE CHANGES COLLEGE OF ARTS AND SCIENCES CSC 440 | Design and Analysis of Algorithms, Effective Spring 2027 Change prerequisites (4 crs.) Algorithm design and analysis, advanced data structures, computational complexity.

Sorting, searching including hashing and balanced trees, string pattern matching, polynomial and matrix calculations, graph and network algorithms, NP-completeness and intractability. (Lec. 4) Pre: CSC212 and one of the following: CSC340, MTH447(CSC447) PHY 401 | Seminar In Physics, Effective Spring 2027 Change course title and/or course description (1 cr.) Preparation and presentation of papers on selected topics in physics. (Seminar) May be repeated for a maximum of 6 credits PHY 402 | Seminar In Physics, Effective Spring 2027 Change course title and/or course description (1 cr.) Preparation and presentation of papers on selected topics in physics. (Seminar) May be repeated for a maximum of 6 credits COLLEGE OF BUSINESS BAI 476 | Machine Learning for Business Intelligence, Effective Spring 2027 Change course title and/or course description, change in method of instruction (3 crs.) An introduction to machine learning for business applications.

Students use Python to build, evaluate, and interpret machine learning models through applied projects such as fraud detection, market segmentation, forecasting demand, with emphasis on real-world decision making. (Lec. 3) Pre: C or better in BAI210 or STA308, and C or better in one of the following: CSC201, CSC310(DSP310), BAI356, BAI405, BAI454.
Or by permission of instructor.

MBA 504 | Financial Management, Effective Spring 2027 Change course title and/or course description (3 crs.) Functions and responsibilities of ﬁnancial managers.
Examination of: ﬁnancial statement analysis, cost of capital, capital structure, valuation, markets, capital budgeting, working capital, mergers, bankruptcy, multinational ﬁnance. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: MBA500, MBA503 or MBA533, and ECN590.
GRADUATE SCHOOL OF OCEANOGRAPHY OCG 601 | Ocean Resilience, Effective Spring 2027 Change course title and/or course description, change prerequisites (3 crs.) Course focuses on complex issues related to changes in the ocean environment.
Topics include climate change, sea level rise, ﬁsheries management, marine pollution, natural hazards and emerging ocean energy initiatives. (Lec/Accelerated Online Program) Pre: Matriculating URI Online Masters of Oceanography student or Ocean Policy and Science Certiﬁcate students, and one of the following: OCG501, OCG521, OCG540 or OCG561.
Or by permission of instructor.

COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING CVE 560 (MCE560) | Applied Finite Element Analysis, Effective Spring 2027 Change course title and/or course description, change in method of instruction (3 crs.) Cross-listed as (CVE) MCE 560.
Direct stiffness method.
Rayleigh-Ritz and Galerkin methods.
Isoparametric elements.
Frames, trusses, plane stress and strain.
Bending of thin plates.
Solve real-world engineering problems using Abaqus and LS-Dyna. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: MCE372 or CVE453, or graduate standing, or permission of instructor.
COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCE CMD 670 | Audiology Residency, Effective Summer 2026 Delete course (6 crs.) Full-time equivalent off campus clinical residency in audiology.
Direct clinical experience with on-site supervision plus oversight by URI faculty.
Placements may vary and combine more than one site. (Externship) May be repeated for a total of 12 credits.
Pre: graduate standing in audiology and completion of CMD 570.

PSY 672 | Individual Clinical Practicum, Effective Spring 2027 Change course title and/or course description, change prerequisites (3 crs.) Introductory experience in dealing with clinical problems in a variety of clinical settings under supervision. (Practicum) May be repeated for a maximum of 15 credits.
S/U credit.
NEW COURSES COLLEGE OF ARTS AND SCIENCES AAF 462 (ENG462) | Contemporary African Poetry & Writing, Effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Cross-listed as (AAF) ENG462.
Exploration of 20th-century African Diaspora poetry, examining themes of (post)coloniality, Black identity, and Pan-Africanism, and will write a collection of poems. (Lec. 3) Pre: ENG105.
May be repeated for a maximum of 6 credits.
SMC 400 | Senior Seminar: Contemporary Issues in Sport & Media, Effective Fall 2027 (3 crs.) Students learn academic theories and practices through engagement with questions and discussions surrounding a contemporary issue in sport and media. (Seminar) Pre: Senior standing or by permission of instructor.
May be repeated for a total of 6 credits.

COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING CVE 510 | Construction Management Principles, Effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Investigates principles of construction project management, including project delivery methods, construction scheduling, cost estimation, and contracting. Introduces leadership skills for managing teams, resolving conflicts, and fostering collaboration in construction projects. (Lec./Online) Pre: Graduate status or permission of instructor. COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND LIFE SCIENCES NRS 565 | Ecological Philosophy, Effective Fall 2026 (3 crs.) Explores philosophical foundations of science with emphasis on ecology. Using historical and contemporary examples, examines scientific thought and ecological debates, highlighting how philosophy shapes research questions, study design, and interpretation. (Seminar) Pre: Graduate standing

UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND FACULTY SENATE Bill #01-02--21 Constitution, By-Laws and University Manual Committee Report #2001-02-2 Constitution Article VII March 8, 2002 Article VII Amendment of the Constitution of the Faculty Senate Recent events demonstrate the desirability of a method for modifying the Faculty Senate Constitution without a referendum to be conducted whenever a change in title of an ex officio member of the Faculty Senate is proposed. The changes to the Amendment Article of the Faculty Senate Constitution recommended in this report are intended to facilitate such modifications while at the same time preserving strong faculty control over the Faculty Senate Constitution. Thus, the CBUM Committee recommends that, in conjunction with the referendums approved recently, a referendum on the following changes to Article VII of the Faculty Senate Constitution be conducted: A. Add to the beginning of VII/1: "Except as provided in VII/3, . . . " VII, paragraph 1, would read (Change in boldface) 1. Except as provided in VII/3, amendments shall be proposed to the General Faculty by a majority of the total voting membership of the Senate, and ratified by an affirmative vote of two-thirds of the General Faculty voting on the question, excluding abstentions, as determined by a mail ballot conducted by the B#01-02--21 http://www.uri.edu/facsen/B#01-02--21.html 1 of 2 1/23/14, 2:03 PM

Executive Committee and by three tellers appointed by the President of the University. B. Add three new paragraphs, VII 3-5: 3. Proposals for changing titles of ex officio members of the Faculty Senate shall be submitted to the Faculty Senate Executive Committee. If in the judgment of the Committee, a title change is of a nature such that incorporating it into the Membership Article (III) of this Constitution does not require a referendum, the Committee shall report this finding to the Faculty Senate, together with a recommendation for an appropriate change of the Membership Article. Unless specified otherwise in the recommendation, the change shall become effective upon a two-thirds majority vote of the senators present and eligible to vote. The recommendation may not be voted upon at the meeting at which it is first moved 4. Any member of the Senate may challenge a finding of the Faculty Senate Executive Committee that a change of the title of an ex officio member of the Faculty Senate can be incorporated into the Faculty Senate Constitution without a referendum. Such a challenge may be presented only prior to the actual vote on the change. If the challenge is upheld by a majority of the senators present and eligible to vote, the title change shall be submitted to the referendum process as outlined in Article VII, 1 and 2, of this Constitution. 5. Changes to the Faculty Senate membership can be made only in accordance with the referendum process as outlined in Article VII, 1 and 2, of this Constitution. NEW PROGRAM REPORT CURRICULUM & STANDARDS COMMITTEE Report 2025-2026-08C At the April 23, 2026 meeting of the Curriculum & Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval. FOR CONFIRMATION BY THE FACULTY SENATE NEW PROGRAMS COLLEGE OF BUSINESS BS – Interdisciplinary Artificial Intelligence, effective Fall 2026 Appendix A The Interdisciplinary & Applied Artificial Intelligence (AI) program prepares students to apply AI technologies ethically, creatively, and effectively to complex real -world challenges. The program is grounded in technical foundations and interdisciplinary collaboration. Students develop hands-on skills in data management, analytics programming, machine learning, v isualization, and generative AI tools. They also examine the broader implications of AI for organizations, work, and society. Emphasis is placed on responsible AI use, human-centered design, and ethical decision-making across contexts. Through project-based coursework, innovation and entrepreneurship experiences, and an applied internship, students learn to work in cross-functional teams and translate AI insights into actionable solutions. Graduates of the program are prepared for roles that require technical fluency and critical thinking, including positions in analytics, innovation, and emerging AI-enabled fields, as well as for graduate study. Major Requirements: BAI110 or EGR101 and EGR106 BAI212 or CSC201 or CSC200 or EGR241 CSC161(DSP161) DSP181G(BIO181G) or EGR316G(PHL316G)

BAI310 or ISE325 BAI356 BAI454 BAI457 or BAI405 or CSC310(DSP310) BAI476 or EGR441 INE349 (2 times with 2 different approved topics) EGR404 or INE349 with an approved topic BAI456 BUS392(IAI392) or ITR302 BAI111 or MTH131 or MTH141or MTH141H BAI210 or STA308 or STA409 or ISE311 WRT290 Professional Electives: Please select two courses from the following: BAI455 MKT467 SCA467 FIN412 FIN431 FIN433 GEO404(OCG404, NRS404) GEO422(NRS422, MAF422) CMB320 CSC521 EGR444 or other approved courses Students must complete a minimum of 55 credits in the major. Free Electives: Two. Students can choose General Education courses and free electives to make up the balance of 120 credits, up to 65 credits. Students must have a minimum GPA of 2.5 to move into the major. A minimum overall GPA of 2.0 and a minimum of 2.0 is required from the required major courses, including all attempts, is required for graduation. A minimum of 120 credits is required for graduation. At least 42 credits must be at the 300-level or above.
